title: Investigate sequencer timeout stall causing 502/504s and implement adaptive guest-quarantine fallback
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Summary: Over the last 36 hours multiple customers reported elevated 502/504 rates and long tail timeouts from the Hosted API. Traces show request sequencing work items getting stuck in the request-sequencer service (the per-tenant ordering/affinity daemon) for multiple seconds, which cascades into upstream proxies issuing fast-fails and amplified client retries. This ticket scopes an investigation and a two-phase remediation: (1) short-term adaptive guest-quarantine and fast-fail policy to protect other tenants and reduce customer-visible 5xxs, (2) medium-term bugfix in the sequencer to prevent stalls and add observability.

Observed behavior:
- Spike of 502/504 and 5xx between 2025-02-26 06:00 and 2025-02-28 02:00 UTC.
- Impacted only Hosted API (no Dedicated or Private clusters observed to be affected).
- Traces show requests entering request-sequencer, hitting a per-tenant queue length > 2k, then a worker goroutine stuck on a KV cache prefetch during multipart prompt assembly for ~5–12s; proxies time out at 3s -> 504.
- Rapid client retries from some SDKs amplified the stall into a tenant-level burst that exhausted sequencer admission slots and upstream connection pools.

Scope & impact:
- Customer-visible: high (multiple enterprise customers reported errors and opened escalations).
- Components: request-sequencer, frontdoor proxy, upstream runtime worker, SDK retry behavior.
- Reproducibility: reproduces under synthetic load that mimics observed multipart prompt patterns + high retry rate.

Short-term mitigation (this ticket):
1) Deploy an admission controller patch at the edge to cap inflight sequenced requests per tenant and return structured 429/503 with Retry-After when burst thresholds are exceeded — reduces cascade of retries.
2) Implement an "adaptive guest-quarantine" route: automatically isolate tenants that exceed safe queue-time or queue-length thresholds for 30s and route them to a lightweight fallback model (lower-cost CPU-backed variant) to keep their traffic alive without blocking the sequencer.
3) Adjust SDK guidance (temporary) to reduce default instant-retries for streaming/text generation to avoid retry storms.

Long-term fix (follow-up):
- Root cause points to a race in the sequencer's prefetch path where a KV prefetch can block on an external shard lease during multipart assembly. We'll instrument the codepath, add timeboxed prefetch with cancellation, and add health metrics for per-tenant sequencing latency distribution.
- Replace blocking prefetch with async-prefetch+promise resolution and bounded concurrency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deploy admission controller with per-tenant caps in prod and confirm 90th percentile platform-wide 5xx rate reduced by >= 70% during controlled repro.
- Adaptive quarantine activates for simulated offending tenant within 10s of threshold breach and fallback route returns success (non-5xx) for >95% of requests for quarantined tenant.
- Sequencer code fix merged with unit+integration tests and can be rolled out with a canary on a small fleet.

Artifacts and links:
- Repro harness and load script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/repro/seq-stall
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/seq/hosted-sequencer-overview
- Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=87654321
- Temporary PR (admission controller + routing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146
- Sequencer fix WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2160

Risk and rollback:
- Admission controller returns 429/503 for high-volume tenants; potential customer impact for the isolated tenant (documented in customer comms). Rollback plan: revert admission gating and toggle quarantine off via feature flag.
